To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel computational approach for the discovery of protective antigenic candidates against mycobacterial infections.

1) the genome scale data is being exploited using innovative system scale strategies to discover protective antigens against mycobacterial pathogenesis; 2) high-throughput technologies are being used for the validation of these antigenic candidates; 3) these antigenic candidates may pave the way for the rational next-generation vaccines and serodiagnoses against mycobacterial infections.
the recent trends in system scale integrative approaches for discovering protective antigens against mycobacterial pathogen have been reviewed in this paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational approaches for the identification of novel protective antigens against mycobacterial infections.
the development of novel approaches for the discovery of protective antigens against mycobacterial diseases.
developing a systems-level understanding of mycobacterial pathogenesis and immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the integration of multiple data sets from various ‘omics’ technologies, along with in vitro validation of antigenicity, is the most promising approach towards the identification of protective antigens for the rational vaccine and diagnostic design.
the system-scale integrative approaches are the need of the hour to combat the mycobacterial infections.
the system scale integrative approach is an emerging trend in the field of mycobacterial immunoproteomics and computational biology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the current state of the art in computational immunoinformatics has been successfully exploited to identify novel protective antigens against mycobacterial infections.
, in silico approaches can provide the much needed boost to the vaccine development and serodiagnosis of mycobacterial pathogens.
the integration of multiple ‘omics’ datasets and computational strategies has been successfully exploited in the identification of novel antigens against mycobacterial infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
system scale strategies can be effectively used to mine the data for the discovery of novel antigenic targets for rational vaccine and serodiagnostic design.

the integration of ‘omics’ and immunoproteomic technologies can provide the much needed insights into the host-pathogen interactions and help to identify novel antigenic candidates that can be exploited to design effective vaccines against these pathogens.
the system scale integrative approaches can be exploited to mine the data for identifying novel protective antigens and to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis.
